# rare punctuation — a single gong boom (silent until gong voice exists).

# the LATE, only addition: one sparse offbeat hat, soft, near the end.

arrangement:
@length 64

0   section call            ; gong + low riff + kick land like a call to the floor
0   in gong
0   in kick
0   in lead
# bars 1-8 equivalent: the riff broods LOW on C2/D#2. nothing added. the emptiness is the hook.

16  section reach-1         ; the riff begins to reach up — F2/F#2 tritone enters. no new tracks.
16  set lead c2 ~ f2 ~  fs2 ~ ~ ~  eb2 ~ ~ ~  c2 ~ ~ ~ c2 ~ f2 ~  fs2 fs2 ~ ~  eb2 ~ c2 ~  ~ ~ ~ ~ c2 ~ ~ ~  eb2 eb2 ~ ~  fs2 ~ ~ ~  eb2 ~ c2 ~ c2 ~ f2 ~  fs2 ~ eb2 ~  c2 ~ ~ ~  eb2 ~ ~ ~ /1

32  section reach-2         ; gong returns once; riff keeps circling higher
32  in gong

48  section reach-3         ; the single sparse hat enters, soft. still never busy.
48  in chh
48  gain chh 0.45 4
# loop: back to the LOW brood = the cycle resets. no drop, no breakdown. the trance is the point.
# NET: the riff EVOLVES BY REACHING UP (low -> tritone), exactly the two-half form in the source.

meta.title: Plastic Dreams (essence portrait, deep tritone)
meta.essence: ONE deep organ riff (register: octave 2, DEEP) on a 4-note C-minor set C2 / D#2(b3) / F2(4) / F#2(#4 tritone blue-note) over a steady four-on-the-floor. The F# tritone is the signature jazzy tension. Form: bars 1-8 brood LOW on C2/D#2 only; bars 9-16 reach UP, adding F2/F#2. Evolution = the riff reaching higher, not layers piling on.
meta.inspiration: Jaydee — 'Plastic Dreams' (1992). COPYRIGHTED work; this is an inspired-by homage using the generic four-on-floor idiom + an ORIGINAL circling riff evoking the deep-organ character, NOT a transcription.
meta.sourceOfTruth: Transcribed from a user-provided Ableton screenshot of a Plastic Dreams recreation ('Main Organ Low' clip, 129 BPM, 4/4, 16-bar loop). Pitch set C2/D#2/F2/F#2 and the low->high two-half form are read directly from the piano roll, not guessed.
meta.pitchSet: C2, D#2 (=eb2), F2, F#2 (=fs2). C minor with the #4 tritone as the hook.
meta.designPrinciple: ESSENCE-FIRST, NOT TEMPLATE. RESTRAINT IS THE RULE. Only kick + the single organ riff + a rare gong. NO chord stabs, NO arp, NO busy hats, NO section-swap drama.

originalInstruments.organ: Renamed to 'lead' here because the engine has no organ voice. Intended timbre: deep drawbar/Hammond, octave 2, stacked sines, percussive attack, slight chorus/vibrato. The register is essential — this riff is felt as much as heard. Synth-voice task, flagged.
originalInstruments.gong: Track kept with original name; currently silent because the engine has no gong voice. 'in gong' cues are no-ops until a voice is added.

essenceNotes.whatChangedVsFailedVersion: Earlier essence guess used c/eb/g/bb (generic minor pentatonic, mid register) and missed it. The REAL riff is an octave lower, on C2/D#2/F2/F#2, and its hook is the F# tritone (#4) plus the low->high two-half form. Harmonizing it 'correctly' before destroyed the character; the actual riff is harmonically weirder and that weirdness IS the hook.
essenceNotes.whyMutationNotLayering: Hypnosis comes from sameness; interest comes from slow change to the SAME element. The riff evolves in place (low->high reach) while the texture stays nearly empty.
essenceNotes.theGong: Punctuation, not groove. Rare hits mark sections like the original's opening gong-call.
essenceNotes.cymaticsCoupling: A near-static spectrum dominated by one octave-2 riff = a steady, slowly-breathing field that shifts subtly as the riff reaches up into the tritone. The visual hypnotism mirrors the musical hypnotism — exactly because nothing busy is competing.

caveats.copyright: Original is copyrighted; this reproduces only the generic four-on-floor idiom + an ORIGINAL riff evoking the character. Homage, not cover.
caveats.swing: House sits slightly behind the grid; the straight 16th grid can't swing (engine feature). Straight here — logged.
caveats.restraintIsFragile: Resist the urge to 'improve' this by adding parts. If it starts sounding busy, the essence is lost. Any addition must be tiny and late.

lessonsForSkill: When a transcription source exists (screenshot/MIDI/score), READ IT — do not harmonize from theory. The real Plastic Dreams riff omits the 5th and 7th and leans on a #4 tritone in octave 2; no amount of 'sensible' minor-pentatonic guessing would have found that. Register and the 'wrong' note are often the essence.
ESSENCE-FIRST RULE: one melodic track, minimal everything else; development by MUTATING the core element, not by adding layers.
Signature timbre is a recurring separate task (Hammond organ at octave 2) — always flag it.
